text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Mubarak says New Delta will open doors to investment in fields of agriculture, industry and tourism until 2017.
- President meets United Nations former secretary general Boutros Boutros-Ghali and attends reception for him. Boutros-Ghali tells Mubarak he is at the service of Egypt and of peace.
- Mubarak tells employees of news and television sectors that there is no alternative to setting up Arab market to deal with economic blocs.
- Ganzouri to tour Toshka area on Monday.
- Egypt condemns terrorist explosion in Damascus. Moussa says Netanyahu's accusations are nonsense and not persuasive.
- Interior Ministry spokesman says letter bombs to Washington are not from Alexandria.
- Mubarak says radio and television sectors will not be privatised.
- Suzanne Mubarak opens village for victims of floods in Luxor and Aswan.
- Public Enterprise minister Atef Obeid says government is committed to getting highest possible price for companies that will go on sale.
- Interior Minister Hassan al-Alfi says terrorist organisations are reorganising.
- Mubarak says Egypt is not inciting Palestinians to delay agreement with Israel.
- Egypt awards grants for southern Sudanese students.
